title: Ch 8 — Exergy
source: Cengel, Boles & Kanoglu — Thermodynamics: An Engineering Approach, Ch. 8
description: Exergy, dead state, exergy of heat, exergy destruction, second-law efficiency.

cards.back: The **maximum useful work** obtainable from a system as it reversibly comes to equilibrium with the environment (the dead state). It measures energy *quality*, not quantity.
Equilibrium with the environment at $T_0$ and $P_0$ (often 25 °C, 1 atm). A system at the dead state has **zero exergy** — no more useful work can be extracted.
No. Unlike energy, exergy is **destroyed** by every irreversibility. Exergy analysis tracks *where* work potential is lost.

cards.front: Exergy of heat transferred from a reservoir at temperature $T$?
cards.back: $X_{heat} = \left(1 - \dfrac{T_0}{T}\right)Q$ — the Carnot-weighted fraction. Heat at $T = T_0$ carries no exergy.

cards.front: Which carries the *most* exergy per unit of energy?
choices: 100 kJ of heat at 400 K ($T_0$ = 300 K)
100 kJ of internal energy at the dead state
cards.back: Work is **entirely** exergy (100% convertible). Heat is only partly exergy ($(1-T_0/T)$), and energy at the dead state has none.

cards.front: Write the *flow exergy* of a stream.
cards.back: $\psi = (h - h_0) - T_0(s - s_0) + \dfrac{V^2}{2} + gz$. The $-T_0(s-s_0)$ term is the unavailable part.
$X_{dest} = T_0\,S_{gen} \ge 0$. Destroyed exergy equals entropy generation times the dead-state temperature.

cards.front: Heat $Q = 1000$ kJ is supplied from a reservoir at **600 K**, with $T_0 = 300$ K. Find its exergy, in kJ.
A process generates $S_{gen} = 0.20$ kJ/(kg·K) with $T_0 = 300$ K. Find the exergy destroyed, in kJ/kg.

cards.back: Exergy recovered ÷ exergy supplied. For work-producing devices $\eta_{II} = W_u/W_{rev}$; for work-consuming ones $\eta_{II} = W_{rev}/W_u$. It compares a device to the reversible ideal for the same task.
